questions.q: What real-world problem does dynamic measure selection solve?
options: Letting a viewer swap which measure drives a view without you building a separate worksheet for every combination
It permanently merges two data sources together
It removes the need for calculated fields entirely
It automatically publishes a workbook to Tableau Server
questions.explain: Instead of building a new worksheet for every measure combination a stakeholder might ask for, one selector parameter plus one CASE calculation covers all of them on a single worksheet.

questions.q: What does the selector parameter's value actually hold?
options: The measure's name, as a string (e.g. "Profit"), not the measure's value itself
The literal numeric value of the currently selected measure
A reference to the underlying database table
Nothing — the parameter is only decorative
questions.explain: The parameter holds a string like "Profit" or "Sales" — it names a measure. The CASE calculation is what bridges that name to the measure's actual value.

questions.q: What does the CASE calculation do in this pattern?
options: Returns the actual value of whichever measure the selector parameter's string currently names
Deletes every other measure from the Data pane
Automatically updates the parameter's list of allowable values
Converts the parameter into a filter
questions.explain: The CASE statement matches the parameter's current string value against each WHEN clause and returns SUM() of whichever measure that string names.

questions.q: What is the main limitation of this technique as the number of selectable measures grows?
options: Every measure must be manually kept in sync between the parameter's list and the CASE statement — adding one to the data source doesn't add it automatically
It stops working entirely after four measures
Tableau enforces a hard limit of two selectable measures
It cannot be used with String parameters
questions.explain: This is a manual, set-it-up-once technique. A new measure added to the data source has to be added to both the parameter's list and the CASE statement by hand, or selecting it silently does nothing.

questions.q: Does the same selector-plus-CASE pattern work for dimensions, not just measures?
options: Yes — a List parameter of dimension names plus a CASE calculation returning the actual dimension value works the same way
No — parameters can only ever reference measures
No — CASE statements only work with numeric data types
Yes, but only for date dimensions
questions.explain: The identical pattern applies to dimensions: a List parameter holding dimension names, and a CASE calculation returning the corresponding dimension's value, droppable onto Color or Detail.
